concept: Monkey D. Luffy is adapted as a rubber-bodied brawler whose stretched Gum-Gum Pistol is the ordinary attack. The three paths separately develop Gear 3's enlarged, forceful blows, Gear 2's speed and an activated burst of speed, and Gear 4's redirected, rapidly recurring punches. These are Tower Defense interpretations, not claims that Luffy attacks track enemies or has these game mechanics. Gear 5 is a later awakened form, not assumed to be available in every story period.

signature.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
signature.adaptation: Luffy stretches and slingshots a punch at a distant opponent. It is the automatic single-projectile base attack; its reach is represented by range, not by an asserted ability to bypass obstacles.

repertoire.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
repertoire.limitation: A stretched punch is not evidence of obstacle bypass or multiple hits.

effects.effect: Luffy stretches and slingshots a punch at an opponent from a distance.
effects.reason: The base attack and its range upgrades represent a stretched punch reaching a target; clear-path delivery remains required.

repertoire.name: Gear 2
repertoire.limitation: Gear 2 increases Luffy's speed and mobility; the design does not implement blood flow, metabolism, or movement around the battlefield.

effects.effect: Luffy increases his speed and mobility.
effects.reason: Gear 2 purchases make his automatic punches occur more frequently.

effects.effect: Gear 2 techniques can make a strike faster and more forceful.
effects.reason: The Gear 2 path develops stronger ordinary punches and a faster ordinary attack.

repertoire.name: Gear 3
repertoire.limitation: The early temporary shrinking drawback is omitted; the supplied account says Luffy later gained better control and no longer suffered the drawbacks.

effects.effect: Luffy inflates a body part to gigantic size to enhance its strength.
effects.reason: The path's heavy enlarged-limb strike deals greater damage and hits nearby enemies through splash, a Tower Defense adaptation of its massive-scale impact.

repertoire.name: Gear 4
repertoire.limitation: Gear 4's Haki expenditure and recovery period are not represented as a separate resource or forced downtime.

effects.effect: Gear 4 forms enhance some combination of defense, speed, and power.
effects.reason: The path permanently develops stronger, faster punches; no defense stat exists in this Definition.

effects.effect: Python redirects punches during an attack and avoids the usual buildup between attacks.
effects.reason: The design represents redirection as a bounded hit on distinct secondary enemies and represents reduced buildup as a faster ordinary attack. It does not steer projectiles or retarget around obstructions.

repertoire.name: Gear 5
repertoire.limitation: This is an awakened later form. The plan does not implement environmental or other-living-being rubberization, free-form imagination, or a general cartoon-physics system.

effects.effect: Luffy's awakened form increases physical power and speed and permits unusually flexible bodily shape and size.
effects.reason: The limited representation is stronger, faster ordinary attacks. The design omits unbounded transformation and environmental effects.

repertoire.name: Observation Haki
repertoire.limitation: Sensing presence or intent does not by itself prove detection of Camo-hidden enemies; this plan does not grant that capability.

effects.effect: Luffy senses presence and intent and can predict opponents' moves.
effects.reason: The Definition has no prediction, evasion, or enemy-intent mechanic, and this plan does not claim Camo detection from this evidence.

repertoire.name: Armament Haki
repertoire.limitation: The plan adapts increased attack force only. Haki's defense and contact with particular intangible opponents have no general enemy-property equivalent established here.

effects.effect: Armament Haki can amplify the force of Luffy's attacks.
effects.reason: The late top-path damage increase is a Tower Defense representation of stronger blows; it does not claim a special damage type or universal defense-negation.

repertoire.name: Supreme King Haki
repertoire.limitation: The plan does not implement a fear-based or will-based area knockout. Infusion is represented only as stronger blows.

effects.effect: Luffy's infusion of Supreme King Haki dramatically increases the power of his attacks.
effects.reason: The late top-path damage increase represents more powerful impacts, without claiming the unimplemented will-based knockout effect.

base.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
base.behavior: At 0-0-0, Luffy stretches and slingshots one normal-damage punch at the player's selected target every attack interval. The attack has the proposed base range and pierce from the supplied Profile scale, with a single shared per-attack hit capacity including the primary target; a given enemy cannot be hit twice by that attack. It requires a clear delivery path and has no Camo detection. These are proposed Tower Defense parameters, not canon quantities.

path1.name: Gear 3 Enlarged Limb
path1.buyFor: Choose this path when a heavier blow and group impact are more valuable than frequent attacks.
path1.weakness: The enlarged strike is slower and its finite hit capacity limits how many enemies one attack can damage. It does not bypass obstacles, and the early-story shrinking drawback is not represented.

milestones.tier1: At 1-x-x, Luffy puts more force into each ordinary stretched punch against the selected target; it remains one clear-path projectile.
milestones.tier2: At 2-x-x, Luffy further strengthens each ordinary punch against the selected target without changing its delivery or single-projectile form.
milestones.tier3: At 3-x-x, Luffy inflates a limb for a heavier, slower ordinary strike; its impact damages enemies near the selected primary target through splash. Primary and splash targets share the attack's finite hit capacity, and no enemy is hit twice by that attack.
milestones.tier4: At 4-x-x, Luffy makes the Gear 3 impact stronger and raises its per-attack hit capacity; primary and nearby splash hits still share that capacity.
milestones.tier5: At 5-x-x, the slower Gear 3 impact becomes still heavier and knocks eligible enemies back briefly when hit. The attack retains its shared finite capacity; Blimps and Bosses ignore knockback.

path1.capstoneValue: The fifth purchase adds a distinct, bounded control effect to the enlarged impact rather than only increasing its damage. One concentrated placement supplies that control alongside Gear 3's splash; it does not control immune targets or remove the attack's capacity limit.

crosspaths.contribution: Proposed early purchases: At x-1-x, Luffy begins throwing the ordinary stretched punch more frequently at the player's selected target; it remains one projectile. At x-2-x, Luffy further increases the frequency of his ordinary single punch against the selected target.

Proposed early purchases: At x-x-1, Luffy stretches his ordinary punch farther toward the player's selected target while retaining clear-path delivery and one projectile. At x-x-2, Luffy's ordinary punch can hit more distinct enemies along its clear path before its per-attack capacity is exhausted; an enemy cannot be hit twice by that attack.

path1.referenceExample: The Profile's scale references inform this proposal; the supplied Definition alone authorizes mechanics.

path2.name: Gear 2 Jet Pistol
path2.buyFor: Choose this path when frequent single-target punches and a timed burst against a priority enemy matter most.
path2.weakness: Its automatic attack remains a single-projectile punch with limited per-attack capacity. The temporary boost is not permanent attack speed and does not shorten its cooldown.

milestones.tier1: At x-1-x, Luffy begins throwing the ordinary stretched punch more frequently at the player's selected target; it remains one projectile.
milestones.tier2: At x-2-x, Luffy further increases the frequency of his ordinary single punch against the selected target.
milestones.tier3: At x-3-x, Luffy uses Gear 2's speed and force to make each ordinary punch stronger and more frequent; the attack remains a single clear-path projectile.
milestones.tier4: At x-4-x, Luffy unlocks one manually activated temporary Gear 2 boost to the purchased ordinary punch, increasing its attack rate for the Active window. The boost changes no target choice, adds no separate attack, and begins its cooldown when activated.
milestones.tier5: At x-5-x, the same Gear 2 Active lasts longer and each boosted punch can follow up against one distinct eligible secondary enemy after its primary hit. This bounded follow-up inherits the attack's existing damage and effects, shares no claim of repeated hits, and does not create another Active.

path2.capstoneValue: The fifth purchase adds a bounded secondary hit to the path's existing Active-boosted attack and extends the boost window. It offers a distinct burst pattern rather than only a larger multiplier; the follow-up is limited to a distinct secondary enemy.

At 2-x-x, Luffy further strengthens each ordinary punch against the selected target without changing its delivery or single-projectile form.

path3.name: Gear 4 Python Redirected Punches
path3.buyFor: Choose this path when sustained attack throughput and hits on additional distinct enemies are preferred over splash or knockback.
path3.weakness: The represented Python follow-up can reach only a bounded number of distinct secondary enemies and does not steer around obstructions. The game model does not represent Gear 4's Haki recovery or defensive benefit.

milestones.tier1: At x-x-1, Luffy stretches his ordinary punch farther toward the player's selected target while retaining clear-path delivery and one projectile.
milestones.tier2: At x-x-2, Luffy's ordinary punch can hit more distinct enemies along its clear path before its per-attack capacity is exhausted; an enemy cannot be hit twice by that attack.
milestones.tier3: At x-x-3, Luffy uses a Gear 4 form's speed to throw ordinary punches more frequently, retaining the player's target choice and the base attack's delivery.
milestones.tier4: At x-x-4, Luffy's Python-like redirection represents reduced buildup between punches: the ordinary attack becomes stronger and faster, while its primary target remains the player's choice.
milestones.tier5: At x-x-5, each ordinary Python punch may hit up to two distinct eligible secondary enemies after its primary target. The follow-up uses the punch's existing damage and effects, does not hit the primary again, does not recursively chain, and does not claim to bend around obstacles.

path3.capstoneValue: The fifth purchase adds a two-target bounded follow-up to Python's redirected attack, a distinct capability beyond faster and stronger punches. Concentrating in this purchase increases the number of distinct secondary enemies reached per attack, not the attack's range or primary targeting control.

At 2-x-x, Luffy further strengthens each ordinary punch against the selected target without changing its delivery or single-projectile form.

omittedTechniques.name: Soru
omittedTechniques.reason: This is a rapid movement technique that lets Luffy move at disappearing speeds. The Definition models stationary attacks, not Luffy's battlefield movement or evasion, and a purchase that needs those behaviors cannot express them as an attack change.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Jet Pistol
omittedTechniques.reason: This is Luffy's Gear 2 version of the Gum-Gum Pistol, with a very fast, forceful punch that propels its target. Its central speed and force are represented by the Gear 2 path and knockback by the Gear 3 path, but no purchase names this exact technique, so it is not claimed as an implemented separate repertoire entry.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Jet Stamp
omittedTechniques.reason: The supplied passage identifies it as the Gear 2 version of Stamp but does not describe its combat effect in the selected evidence. No specific behavior can be safely adapted from that naming alone.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Jet Bazooka
omittedTechniques.reason: The supplied passage identifies it as the Gear 2 version of Bazooka but the selected evidence does not describe its attack effect. A separate attack behavior cannot be inferred from its name.

omittedTechniques.name: Hone Fusen
omittedTechniques.reason: The described technique inflates Luffy's body for defense and can ricochet bullets, but the Definition has no defensive or projectile-reflection mechanic for this Unit. Its central defensive behavior therefore is not adapted.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Gigant Pistol
omittedTechniques.reason: This is Gear 3's giant version of Gum-Gum Pistol. The Gear 3 path adapts the form's described enlarged, massive-scale impact, but the exact named attack is not separately implemented; the selected passage naming it does not itself establish further behavior.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Rocket
omittedTechniques.reason: The passage identifies a launch movement used to compensate for Gear 3 mobility disadvantage, but the Definition does not model movement or repositioning. No attack or obstacle-bypass effect is inferred.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Gigant Axe
omittedTechniques.reason: The selected evidence names this Gear 3 attack but does not provide its combat effect. The path represents Gear 3's general enlarged impact, not an unsubstantiated axe-specific delivery.

omittedTechniques.name: Kin'niku Fusen
omittedTechniques.reason: The described Gear 4 technique inflates Luffy's muscular structure and enhances durability, but the Definition has no defense or damage-mitigation mechanic. Its central defensive behavior is not implemented.

omittedTechniques.name: Atama Buso
omittedTechniques.reason: The evidence describes hardening Luffy's forehead and preparing for a headbutt, but does not describe a distinct attack effect. This plan does not claim a headbutt purchase or invent its damage behavior.

omittedTechniques.name: Gear 2 Buso
omittedTechniques.reason: The evidence describes Luffy hardening a fist during Gear 2 and an apparent ignition effect. No purchase adapts the burning effect, and this design does not claim flame damage from the passage's qualified wording.

omittedTechniques.name: Afro Luffy
omittedTechniques.reason: The claimed extra power is presented as a joke or possibly playful agreement, and the form appears only once in the original manga. It does not support a reliable combat mechanic.

omittedTechniques.name: Nightmare Luffy
omittedTechniques.reason: The form depends on containing shadows and using their combined strength and skills, with a limited duration. The supplied Definition has no shadow acquisition, summoning, combined-skill, or transformation resource mechanic, so its central source-dependent behavior cannot be represented by this plan.

scopeLimits: The supplied evidence is a bounded selection, not a complete repertoire survey; this plan does not claim exhaustive coverage or independent canon verification.

Gum-Gum Pistol, Gear 2 and Gear 3 are supported as Luffy techniques; Gear 4 and Gear 5 have their own period and prerequisite context in the supplied passages. The design does not assert that every story period has access to every form.

The supplied Definition has no defense, immunity, evasion, environmental rubberization, free-form reality alteration, fear or will-based knockout, or character movement mechanics. These effects are not silently converted into ordinary damage.

The supplied Definition cannot model redirected projectile trajectories, attacks that bypass obstacles, Haki resource exhaustion, Gear 4 recovery, or early Gear 3 shrinking. Those behaviors are not promised.
All numerical values, upgrade effects, capacities, durations and prices are proposals subject to implementation and playtesting; this response makes no claim of engine support or balance.
